title: Exact String Match
description: Exact matching finds occurrences identical to the pattern, character for character — the foundation of search boxes, find-in-page, and key lookups. The naive scan is O(n*m); the Knuth-Morris-Pratt algorithm reaches O(n+m) by never re-scanning text after a mismatch. The demo below runs a real KMP search in JavaScript.
demo:
function kmp(t,p){const l=[0];for(let i=1;i<p.length;i++){let j=l[i-1];while(j>0&&p[i]!==p[j])j=l[j-1];if(p[i]===p[j])j++;l.push(j);}const out=[];let j=0;for(let i=0;i<t.length;i++){while(j>0&&t[i]!==p[j])j=l[j-1];if(t[i]===p[j])j++;if(j===p.length){out.push(i-j+1);j=l[j-1];}}return out;}
console.log('KMP find "ana" in "banana":', kmp('banana','ana'));
provenance: Public reference: standard string-algorithm and information-retrieval literature; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Prefix and Suffix Match
description: Prefix matching (starts-with) powers autocomplete; suffix matching (ends-with) powers file-type detection and domain checks. Tries make prefix search over millions of keys fast by sharing common prefixes. The demo runs both over a word list.
provenance: Public reference: standard string-algorithm and information-retrieval literature; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Fuzzy Match (Levenshtein)
description: Fuzzy matching tolerates typos: the Levenshtein distance counts the minimum insertions, deletions, and substitutions turning one string into another. Spell checkers and 'did you mean' features rank candidates by this distance. The demo computes the classic dynamic-programming distance between 'kitten' and 'sitting' (answer: 3).
provenance: Public reference: standard string-algorithm and information-retrieval literature; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Regular Expression Match
description: Regular expressions describe pattern families — character classes, repetitions, groups — compiled to finite automata for linear-time matching. They validate emails, parse logs, and lex programming languages. The demo validates and extracts with a real regex.
provenance: Public reference: standard string-algorithm and information-retrieval literature; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Glob and Wildcard Match
description: Glob patterns use * (any run) and ? (one character) for filename-style matching — the language of shell wildcards and .gitignore rules. Simpler than regex but exactly right for paths and names. The demo converts a glob to a regex and tests it.
provenance: Public reference: standard string-algorithm and information-retrieval literature; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Phonetic Match (Soundex)
description: Phonetic matching encodes how names sound: Soundex (1918, for census records) maps 'Smith' and 'Smyth' to the same code S530, catching spelling variants in genealogy and record linkage. Metaphone and Double Metaphone refine it. The demo implements real Soundex.
demo:
function soundex(s){const m={b:1,f:1,p:1,v:1,c:2,g:2,j:2,k:2,q:2,s:2,x:2,z:2,d:3,t:3,l:4,m:5,n:5,r:6};s=s.toUpperCase();let code=s[0],prev=m[s[0]]||0;for(const ch of s.slice(1)){const d=m[ch]||0;if(d&&d!==prev)code+=d;prev=d;if(code.length===4)break;}return (code+'000').slice(0,4);}
console.log('Smith:',soundex('Smith'),'Smyth:',soundex('Smyth'),'match:',soundex('Smith')===soundex('Smyth'));
provenance: Public reference: standard string-algorithm and information-retrieval literature; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Semantic Match (Token Overlap)
description: Semantic matching compares meaning, not spelling: token-overlap and cosine similarity over word vectors rank 'car for sale' near 'automobile listing' despite sharing no words. Modern systems use embedding vectors; the demo shows the classical Jaccard-over-tokens version that still powers baseline search.
demo:
function jaccard(a,b){const A=new Set(a.toLowerCase().split(/\W+/)),B=new Set(b.toLowerCase().split(/\W+/));const inter=[...A].filter(x=>B.has(x)).length;return inter/(A.size+B.size-inter);}
console.log('jaccard("red sports car","red fast automobile") =', jaccard('red sports car','red fast automobile').toFixed(2));
provenance: Public reference: standard string-algorithm and information-retrieval literature; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Visual Match (Perceptual Hash)
description: Visual matching finds near-duplicate images by perceptual hash: shrink to 8x8 grayscale, compare each pixel to the average, and emit 64 bits — images differing only by resize or slight recompression hash within a few bits of each other. Reverse image search and duplicate detection run on this idea. The demo hashes two tiny pixel grids and compares Hamming distance.
provenance: Public reference: standard string-algorithm and information-retrieval literature; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Audio Match (Fingerprint Concept)
description: Audio fingerprinting (the Shazam method) finds matching songs from short clips: it extracts spectral peaks from a spectrogram, hashes pairs of peaks with their time offsets, and looks the hashes up in a database — robust to noise, EQ, and compression. The demo simulates the peak-pair hashing idea on synthetic peak lists.
provenance: Public reference: standard string-algorithm and information-retrieval literature; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Structural Match (JSON Path)
description: Structural matching navigates nested data by shape: JSONPath ($.store.book[?(@.price<10)]) and XPath query trees the way regex queries text. Config validators and API testers match on structure rather than string content. The demo walks a real nested object with a tiny path evaluator.
provenance: Public reference: standard string-algorithm and information-retrieval literature; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Anagram Match
description: Anagram matching detects rearrangements — 'listen' versus 'silent' — by comparing sorted characters or character-count signatures. Word games, plagiarism detectors, and license-plate puzzles use it. The demo builds canonical signatures and groups anagrams.
provenance: Public reference: standard string-algorithm and information-retrieval literature; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Palindrome Match
description: Palindrome matching finds strings reading the same backward — 'racecar,' 'nurses run' — used in DNA sequence analysis (inverted repeats) and word puzzles. The two-pointer check runs in linear time with constant space. The demo tests several candidates with normalization.
demo:
function isPal(s){s=s.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g,'');let i=0,j=s.length-1;while(i<j){if(s[i++]!==s[j--])return false;}return true;}
console.log('racecar:',isPal('racecar'),'| nurses run:',isPal('nurses run'),'| hello:',isPal('hello'));
provenance: Public reference: standard string-algorithm and information-retrieval literature; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Subsequence Match
description: Subsequence matching asks whether the pattern's characters appear in order (not necessarily adjacently) — the logic behind fuzzy file finders where 'fb' matches 'foobar.' It runs in linear time with a single scan. The demo powers a tiny fuzzy-finder ranking.
provenance: Public reference: standard string-algorithm and information-retrieval literature; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Normalized Case-Insensitive Match
description: Normalized matching folds case, strips accents, and trims whitespace before comparing — so 'Café', 'café', and 'CAFE' all match. Search boxes and login systems depend on it; Unicode casefold plus NFKD normalization handles the edge cases naive lowercasing misses. The demo shows the full pipeline.
demo:
function norm(s){return s.normalize('NFKD').replace(/[\u0300-\u036f]/g,'').toLowerCase().trim();}
console.log(norm('  Café '), '===', norm('CAFE'), ':', norm('  Café ')===norm('CAFE'));
provenance: Public reference: standard string-algorithm and information-retrieval literature; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Multi-Pattern Match (Aho-Corasick)
description: Multi-pattern matching finds many patterns in one pass: the Aho-Corasick automaton (1975) builds a trie of all patterns with failure links, scanning text once in O(n + m + z) — the engine behind antivirus signature scanning and content filters. The demo scans for three keywords simultaneously.
provenance: Public reference: standard string-algorithm and information-retrieval literature; verified 2026-10-21.
